body:
`helper.book_cover_is_locked` (cps/helper.py) swallows every exception and returns `False`:

    try:
        record = ub.session.query(ub.BookCoverLock).filter_by(book_id=book_id).first()
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive; missing migrations etc.
        return False

Every caller reads that as "not locked" and writes the cover. So on any error reaching the lock
table, the guard silently does the opposite of its purpose and a deliberately-locked cover is
overwritten with no signal at all. Three call sites depend on it: the classic editor
(editbooks.py), the ingest auto-metadata fetch (metadata_helper.py), and — as of the #1971 fix —
the SPA cover endpoint.

The comment names the intended case, "missing migrations", and for that case fail-open is genuinely
correct: if the `book_cover_lock` table does not exist then nobody can have set a lock, so
answering "not locked" is the right answer. But a bare `except Exception` also covers a locked
database, a detached or rolled-back session, a transient I/O error, and an ordinary bug — cases
where a lock DOES exist and the user's explicit decision is discarded.

Fix shape: distinguish the two. Treat a missing table as unlocked; treat any other failure as
locked — skipping the cover is the safe direction for all three callers — and log it. Leaving it
fail-open is defensible only if it is written down, because today the behaviour is invisible and
every caller reads the helper as a guarantee.

Found by an adversarial review of #1971, which added the third caller. Deliberately not fixed
there: changing a shared helper's failure semantics affects two other write paths and deserves its
own change and its own release note.
title: book_cover_is_locked fails OPEN, so a failing lock query silently permits the overwrite it exists to prevent
